Zone IV is one of five planning zones in Islamabad Capital Territory — attractions here are grouped by zone rather than by separate towns.

history.founded: Designated as one of Islamabad's rural development zones on the city's eastern/southern edge
history.city_history: Zone IV consists largely of rural and semi-rural land on Islamabad's periphery, with scattered farming communities and some newer housing developments.
history.province_history: Islamabad was purpose-built starting in 1960 as Pakistan's new capital, replacing Karachi, and was inaugurated in 1967. Designed by Greek architect Constantinos Doxiadis on a grid of numbered sectors at the foot of the Margalla Hills, it is one of the few purpose-planned capital cities in South Asia.
